variant.title: Minimal · halo
variant.summary: Simple: NO moving heads, the rental house's fixed lights only (UP-PL5403 PARs, UP-COB200 COB PARs). Minimal's hall; a flat triangle of 3 x 4 m truss at 6 m under the crane bridge over the DJ, apex to the crowd, 3 hoists on bridles. 8 PARs round it focused IN to a ring round the DJ (the cone), the apex PAR straight down (the pillar), the base corners' PARs crossing over the DJ (the X), 4 PARs out to the crowd, 4 red PARs grazing the bridge, 4 COBs on it and 4 in the pit for the hits; the columns and the press in red.

assumptions: The DJ place (the owner's green, 2026-09-28) is a riser of stage decks 3 m wide x 2 m deep x 1.2 m high ON THE NAVE CENTRE LINE (x 0; the owner, 04:13: 'make the scene in center'), its back edge 1.0 m in front of the press's face (z 3.2 m, +-1.5 m), facing the entry and the crowd. The press stays where it stands, 1.65 m right of the axis (range 0.5-3.5), behind the right half of the riser. Three 2 x 1 m decks on 1.2 m legs; 'a bit top' read as 1.0-1.4 m. Options considered: stage.options (D chosen).

The DJ stands behind a 1.8 x 0.8 m DJ table, 0.95 m high, at the riser's front edge; treads up the left side (toward the backstage); a crowd barrier 1.3 m in front of the riser, 9 m long. The crowd (blue) fills the floor from the barrier to under the crane.

The machinery stays the backdrop: the press (to 5.3 m) stands behind the right half of the riser and the machine line beside it further right, so from the floor the DJ is seen against the press; the goalpost header at 7 m is above the press's crown.

No stage deck, no towers: the DJ stand alone. A flat equilateral triangle of 290 mm square box truss (Global Truss F34; Prolyte H30V is the same class), 4 m a side, lies at 6 m (bottom chord) centred under the crane bridge over the DJ, its apex toward the audience, on 3 chain hoists (one per corner, each on a two-leg bridle) with safety steels; load ≈ 264 kg, corners 92 / 86 / 86 kg (apex / left / right). rigging sign-off owed (crane rated load, lock-out, hoists + safety steels).

Strobes, blinders and hazers are other-supplier lines (the rental house lists none): each is a planning type modelled on a named product (scripts/place/fixtures/fixtures.json, EXT- codes). No CO2 jet, cold spark or confetti — the underground brief (versions file, method).

Each LOOK is one static state for previsualisation (a focus palette), not a show: positions are the rig's, aims and colours the look's. Every lamp but the press's own six mirrors about the nave centre line (x 0), the booth's axis too. Brightness between fixtures follows the datasheets (photometry below); the overall exposure is one chosen number (photometry.sceneScale).

truss.why: Option 6 of the ten truss versions, built as a comparison beside option 4 on Minimal. The triangle is the object; the lamps live on it.
truss.section_class: 290 mm square box truss (Global Truss F34; Prolyte H30V is the same class)
truss.corner: Global Truss F34 C20 2-way corner 60° (F34C20: 8.80 kg, outer 1000 x 1000 x 290 mm)
truss.corner_source: https://globaltruss.de/en/F34-2-way-corner-C20-600/F34C20 (opened 2026-09-29): "F34 2-way corner C20 60° … Weight: 8,80 kg … Dimensions (L/W/H): 1000 x 1000 x 290 mm". A 60° corner is a STANDARD catalogue part of the 290 mm system (the same series lists C19 45°, C21 90°, C22 120°, C23 135°).
truss.corner_leg_why: The page gives the C20's outer box, not its leg on the centre line. 0.5 m is ASSUMED so a side = 0.5 + 3 m F34300 + 0.5 = 4.0 m node to node; read the real leg from Global Truss's 'DWG files (F34 System)' on the same page before ordering (a longer leg makes the side longer — stock straights only).
truss.orientation: Apex toward the crowd (+z), base edge behind the DJ under the bridge's back girder.
truss.orientation_why: (1) The base edge lies behind the DJ and 0.3 m clear of the press in plan (its truss z 3.50-3.79; the press ends at z 3.2), so nothing hangs over the machine; with the apex toward the press, the triangle's point would sit 0.25 m off the press's left edge and a side would cross over its corner. (2) From the floor the apex points at the people and the two long sides run back to frame the DJ against the press — the halo reads as an arrowhead opening onto the performer. (3) Either way one corner lies beyond the bridge (the triangle is 3.46 m deep, the two girders span 2.9 m face to face); the apex is one pick, the base would be two.

rigging.hoist: chain hoist 500 kg, BGV-D8+ (e.g. ChainMaster D8Plus 500 kg SK030/76U; CM Lodestar class)
rigging.hoist_source: ChainMaster D8Plus 500 kg data sheet: 'Weight (without chain): approx. 20 kg', chain 0.59 kg/m (P5.4 x 15)
rigging.per_point: Each corner: a two-leg bridle (a V, legs ±0.75 m, 0.75 m deep: 90° between the legs, each leg ≈ 0.71 x the pick) on beam clamps, a chain hoist hook-suspended under its ring, the chain and a round sling round the corner block; a safety steel from the corner to the crane, independent of the hoist. Base corners: the V along the back girder (it holds x). Apex: the V along the outrigger (it holds z). Three V's in two directions hold the halo in x, z and in turn.
rigging.crane: the nave's entry-end bridge crane, rolled along its runway to park over the DJ; rail height 7.6 m (disputed 6.6-8.4), girder bottom 8.15 m, two 0.7 m box girders at ±1.1 m
rigging.signoff: rigging sign-off owed (crane rated load, lock-out, hoists + safety steels): the crane's rated load and a check of the old runway, rails and brakes; the crane locked in place and its power isolated for the whole event; the apex OUTRIGGER is a cantilever off the bridge (its back clamps are pulled up) and needs a structural engineer's check or a different pick (a bridle to the roof steel, or a 3 m halo that fits under the bridge); a rigger's plan with the point loads, signed by a structural or rigging engineer. This file draws it; they approve it.

sway.concern: Owner, 2026-09-29: moving heads may swing a chain-hung truss.
sway.method: A chain-hung load is a pendulum, T = 2π√(L/g), L = pivot to the load's centre of mass. Out of a bridle's plane the pivot is the girder; in its plane the V is triangulated (stiff). The three V's lie in two directions (x at the base, z at the apex), so the halo is held in x, z and turn; the pendulum below is the bound if a bridle is left out.

rule.text: No head moves full range faster than 4 s (every cue that moves a halo head fades ≥ 4 s; a strobe hit moves nothing); no periodic movement (a chase, a sweep FX) with a period between 1.5 and 6 s — half to twice the pendulum's period — on the halo's heads; heads reposition in black.

sway.tie_offs: Not drawn: with the three bridles none is needed on paper. If the rigger wants more, tie the base corners back to the crane girders with horizontal ratchet straps — never to the crowd floor.
sway.fixed: This version has NO moving heads: nothing on the halo moves, so no head's reaction can set it swinging (the pendulum numbers stay for the heads version).

effects.label: hazer
effects.note: 2 hazers on the floor behind the line, either side of the booth: the haze rolls from behind the DJ over the floor

budget.why: A browser cannot run ~90 real three.js spot lights: each is a term in the shader of every lit pixel and, with shadows on, a shadow render and a texture unit each (WebGL gives 16-32; past that every lit material fails to compile). Every fixture draws its beam cone; only these 8 lamps also light the room (the rest of the PARs' light on the columns and the press is baked, wash-glb.mjs), and shadows are OFF by default (the owner found the first version too laggy, 2026-09-27). Measured — see scripts/place/README.md, 'The rig'.
budget.realNote: 2026-09-28 (DJ place): the press's own uplights stand 0.35 m from it, where a real lamp in the renderer blows the face out white; they are baked like the other PARs, and the 4 header spots (6.3 m up, over the DJ and the press) are the real lamps that light the backdrop.

night.note: Darker than the base's readable night (ambient 0.8 -> 0.5, directional 0.35 -> 0.22): darkness is part of the design here (rule 1); the hall must still read in a render. Tuned by eye on the RTX 3080, 2026-09-28.

photometry.method: scripts/place/rig-lib.mjs, 'PHOTOMETRY': candela from the manifest (I = E*d^2 from a measured illuminance, else I = flux / beam solid angle); zoom keeps flux; three.js SpotLight intensity is candela x sceneScale; beam-in-air brightness ~ I*tan(theta/2), scaled to the brightest class, Stevens exponent 1/3, times `air`.
photometry.sceneScaleNote: ONE exposure number for the whole rig, chosen so the room reads in a browser's tone mapping (ACES, exposure 1). The ratios between fixtures are the datasheets'.
photometry.airNote: how much haze is in the air: the brightest class's beam gets this `haze` (0..1, src/objectComponents/spotBeam.js).
photometry.airWhy: Heavy haze (rule 4; 2-6 hazers in every version where the base had 4 smoke machines): every cone's air brightness at 1.5 where the base rig draws 0.9. A drawing choice, not photometry — the ratios between the fixtures stay the datasheets'.

halo-one-beam.title: Blackout + one beam
halo-one-beam.intent: Everything out but one: the apex PAR straight down — a white pillar in the pit between the crowd and the DJ, who stands behind it as a shape.

halo-slow-sweep.title: Slow sweep
halo-slow-sweep.intent: Fixed lights cannot sweep: the halo OPENS instead — the 4 PARs behind the DJ throw out over his head to the crowd in cold white, the columns and the bridge glow low red. On the desk this is a slow chase across the four (never a move: nothing moves).

halo-red-room.title: Red room
halo-red-room.intent: Deep red and low: the cone's 8 PARs at half in red make a red cage round the DJ, the two base-corner PARs cross in a red X over his head, the columns, the press and the bridge glow red from below; the roof stays black.

halo-white-cathedral.title: White cathedral
halo-white-cathedral.intent: The cone on the DJ: the 8 PARs round the halo at full cold white close in to a ring round him — a cone of light with the performer inside it, the pillar in front; everything else dark.

halo-strobe-hit.title: Strobe hit
halo-strobe-hit.intent: The peak: the 8 COBs (4 on the halo, 4 in the pit) at full in their strobe mode, every PAR out, so the hit lands on black.

show.why: Minimal's five cues, fades and holds (one 60 s pass). Fixed lights: nothing moves, so the sway rule is met by construction; only levels and colours change.

opening.note: the first screen of the crane rig: 14 m out on the dance floor, on the centre line, eye height, looking up to 5.2 m so the crane bridge and the line hung under it frame the DJ, the press glowing behind (tuned by looking, 2026-09-28 night: at 20 m / 4.6 m the bridge read small over an empty floor)
